scopeBasis.geography: accessible.org/pricing names no country as the basis for its prices. It mentions ADA and EAA compliance, EN 301 549, and a San Antonio TX footer address, so US is implied but not stated.
scopeBasis.timeframe: Page footer: 'Pricing information accurate and updated on October 29, 2026.' This is current.
scopeBasis.population: The figure is for 'most clients'. The page says its clients range 'from Fortune 500 companies to local governments to small businesses', so this is not a small-business price.
scopeBasis.definitions: This is the vendor's own published remediation price per engagement, i.e. a price per sale that this vendor charges. It is available only after an Accessible.org audit with full code access.

verdicts.note: The exact sentence is under 'Accessibility Remediation Cost': '$750 – $4,500 for most clients, $100 – $450 per page or screen, depending on volume and complexity.' The table row shows only '$750 – $4,500'. The claim is supported, but it is one vendor's price across all its clients, not a small-business market price.

verdicts.note: The sentence appears verbatim as the last paragraph under 'Why ADA Website Compliance Feels Out of Reach for Small Businesses'. It supports an upper bound on this one vendor's small-business quotes. It gives no figure for what was paid, and it does not say what the quote covers.

scopeBasis.definitions: This is a price range for a manual WCAG 2.1 AA audit, i.e. a price per sale for an audit (no remediation). It is stated as a general range: 'Pricing varies by provider, page count...'.

verdicts.note: The sentence is verbatim under 'How Much Does an Audit Cost for a Small Site?'. The same article contradicts it twice: 'a focused audit on a small informational site often falls between $500 and $1,000', and its table says 'informational sites often fall between $500 and $1,000 for a WCAG 2.1 AA audit (100% fully manual)'. The claim is accurately quoted, but the page is internally inconsistent about the price for this population.
